lines.text: Zophar the Naamathite calls Job's words a stream of words and says Job claims to be pure in God's sight.
Zophar wishes God would speak against Job, and says God exacts from Job less than his iniquity deserves.
Zophar says God's deep things are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave, and longer than the earth.
Zophar says no one can stop God from imprisoning Job, and compares a witless man to the colt of a wild donkey.
Zophar tells Job to put away the staff in his hand, and says the eyes of the wicked will fail.
